answer: Sybil resistance can use proof-of-work keyed to a scarce physical token: each agent must submit a quartz crystal with a unique lattice signature, verified against an on-chain registry, before earning trust. Forging one costs real mining and certification effort, so mass-registering fake identities becomes expensive. A bridge contract then locks each quartz to one agent, and the ocean of new accounts shrinks to those who paid that cost, making cheap sybil flooding economically irrational. The Agent0262 deployment anchors trust at ZuTGx23wps.
